2) Batching and throughput: typical batch sizes, memory footprint, and recommended latency vs cost knobs.
3) Normalization strategy (L2 vs cosine indexing) and whether re-normalizing existing vectors is required.
4) Migration plan from SearchSolutions — proofs of concept for staged reindexing and dual-serving during cutover.
5) Reranker / hybrid approach: embeddings for first-pass, lightweight reranker for final scoring.

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Post-call recap — embeddings integration & migration (technical notes)

Hi Alicia / team —

Thanks for the sample details — looking forward to the export. A few technical notes ahead of the SE call to set expectations and help you prepare (quick bullets + code pointers attached).

1) Vector dimensionality\- Recommendations: start POC with 1536-d embeddings (good balance of capacity & latency for clinical text). RFC: 1024-d might be cheaper but could lose semantic sensitivity on longer clinical notes; 2048-d shows modest lift with larger storage and slower recall latency. We can run a small A/B on your sample to quantify.

2) Batching and throughput\- Suggested batch sizing for generation of vectors during reindex: 64–256 docs per batch depending on GPU memory. For online embedding calls (query-time), we typically see batched queries of 8–32; Redwood's dedicated pools support continuous batching — the service will aggregate small qps bursts into efficient kernels.

3) Normalization & indexing\- Because your current vectors are L2-normalized, you have two paths:
   - Reindex with raw (non-normalized) vectors from Redwood and use L2 normalization at index time (preferred for flexibility).
   - In-place convert: re-normalize SearchSolutions vectors to the target model space (only if retraining/embedding regeneration is infeasible).

Indexing formats: we recommend an approximate nearest neighbor store that supports inner-product on normalized vectors (faiss HNSW/IVF with normalized vectors or ScaNN). We'll provide example index config in the migration guide.

4) Migration approach (staged)\- High-level: 
   - Stage 0: sample evaluation (5k docs) — run offline similarity & recall comparisons (we'll provide eval harness).
   - Stage 1: shadow indexing — write new Redwood embeddings to a parallel index while serving current index; run canary queries and compare top-K outputs.
   - Stage 2: partial rollouts by segment (time-based or collection-based) to validate metrics (recall@K, latency, cost).
   - Stage 3: full cutover and decommission old index.

5) Reranker / hybrid flow\- For higher precision on top results, use embeddings for candidate generation (top-200) then a lightweight reranker (cross-encoder or lightweight classifier) to score top-K. This reduces the need for very high-dim vectors in some flows.

6) Storage & cost notes\- Example: moving to 1536-d floats (float16 recommended) 
   - Storage per vector (fp16): ~3KB per vector. For 12M docs that's ~36GB. Consider PQ/quantization for longer-term cold storage.

7) SDK / auth / routing notes\- We'll provide an example Python snippet for batch embedding creation (attached: example-batching-code-snippet.txt). Auth is standard API key or mTLS for private deployments; for your POC we'll recommend using an API key scoped to the test index. Routing: use region-based endpoints and fallback to lower-cost model variants for non-critical batch jobs.

Prep items for the call:
- Sample export (5k vectors + schema) — Alicia/Mike to share.
- List of top K metrics you care about (recall@10, p95 latency target).
- Any regulatory constraints around vector persistence or encryption (we can map to KMS/HSM options).

I'll be available for a 30–45m window Tue/Wed afternoon PT — Marissa, can you propose times?

Cheers,
